necessity_evidence.reason: The unpack format supports retained-reference extraction with O, but every unpack call in the fixed entry uses borrowed o. This is a target coverage gap with the same blocker before and after the source change.
necessity_evidence.finite_witness: Input bytes 00 7b 7d: the first byte selects variant 0 and the remaining bytes are the valid JSON object {}. The entry reaches its object unpack calls, whose fixed formats cannot select O.

scope_contract.reason: json_unpack is a primary entry operation, and O is a distinct supported format with a retained-reference result.

feasible_trigger.reason: A valid JSON object can reach the entry's unpack operation. O extraction of that object is supported with a valid output pointer and release of the acquired reference, while the entry fixes the format to o.

observable_consequence.reason: The entry cannot reach O's reference increment or retained-reference extraction through any input; its unpack calls select o.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete entry fixes all three unpack formats to o. Deep copying produces a separate result and does not extract a retained reference to the selected value; object iteration and the other entry operations also do not select O.

evidence.dependency_reason: Deep copying returns its own result, so that entry call is not retained extraction through O.

identity_preserved.reason: Both source versions give O the same reference-incrementing extraction contract, and the same fixed harness selects only o on both sides. The obligation is preexisting.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Distinguishes deep copying from retained extraction of the selected value.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Identifies the separate deep-copy call considered as an alternative route.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: json_unpack with O assigns the selected JSON value and increments its reference count.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Parse a valid JSON value, unpack it with O into a json_t pointer, and release the acquired reference.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: The entry parses fuzzer supplied JSON, then calls json_unpack only with o, {s?o}, and [o!].
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: Retained-reference extraction through O cannot be reached by changing the input bytes.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: None in the complete entry; borrowed o extraction, object iteration, and deep copying do not perform O extraction.

location.dependency_reason: json_unpack passes flags zero, so the entry also cannot enable JSON_STRICT through this wrapper.
The selected json_unpack wrapper passes zero flags.

groups.operation: Unpack an object member with a typed string format and an error destination.
groups.condition: The selected member has the wrong type.
groups.capability: Report a wrong-type diagnostic that includes the object member key; json_unpack provides no error destination.
groups.consequence: The keyed diagnostic cannot be observed through the fixed entry.
groups.equivalence_reason: This concerns the changed diagnostic content and requires an error destination.

groups.operation: Validate an object member while unpacking it with a typed string format.
groups.condition: The selected member is not a string.
groups.capability: Reject the member through string type validation; the fixed entry uses {s?o}, whose o format accepts the value without that check.
groups.consequence: The wrong-type member is not rejected by the fixed entry.
groups.equivalence_reason: This concerns type validation itself, which is distinct from reporting the member key in a diagnostic.

groups.operation: Unpack an object member with a string format and capture the error through json_unpack_ex.
groups.condition: The selected member has a non-string value.
groups.capability: Report a wrong-type diagnostic that names the member key.
groups.consequence: The keyed diagnostic cannot be observed through the entry's json_unpack calls, which provide no error destination.
groups.equivalence_reason: Both describe the same keyed diagnostic for a wrong-type string member and its required error destination.

groups.operation: Unpack an object member with a string format.
groups.condition: The selected member has a non-string value.
groups.capability: Validate the member as a string; the entry's {s?o} format selects the type-insensitive o case.
groups.consequence: The non-string member is not rejected by string validation.
groups.equivalence_reason: Both describe rejection of the same non-string object member under a string format.

groups.operation: Unpack an array element with i.
groups.condition: The selected element is not an integer.
groups.capability: Apply integer validation; the entry's [o!] format selects o.
groups.consequence: The element is not rejected by integer validation.
groups.equivalence_reason: Singleton: array integer validation is a distinct operation.

groups.operation: Unpack a required object member.
groups.condition: The object lacks data.
groups.capability: Reject a missing required member; the entry's ? marker makes data optional.
groups.consequence: The missing data member is not rejected as required.
groups.equivalence_reason: Singleton: required-member validation has a distinct trigger and consequence.

groups.operation: Unpack an object in strict mode.
groups.condition: The object has a member absent from the format.
groups.capability: Reject unrecognized object members using ! or a strict flag.
groups.consequence: The extra member is not rejected by strict object checking.
groups.equivalence_reason: Singleton: strict object-member checking is distinct from type and presence validation.

groups.operation: Unpack an object member as a string using json_unpack_ex.
groups.condition: The selected member has a non-string value and an unpack error destination is supplied.
groups.capability: The string validator receives the object member key and reports a keyed wrong-type diagnostic.
groups.consequence: Without typed validation or an error destination, the keyed diagnostic cannot be observed.
groups.equivalence_reason: Both describe the same string-member mismatch and keyed diagnostic.

groups.operation: Unpack an object member with a string format.
groups.condition: The selected member is not a string.
groups.capability: The string format validates the member type instead of accepting it through o.
groups.consequence: A fixed {s?o} format cannot reject the member for having the wrong type.
groups.equivalence_reason: Both describe the same object-member string validation.

groups.operation: Unpack an array element with i.
groups.condition: The element is not an integer.
groups.capability: The i format validates the element type.
groups.consequence: A fixed [o!] format cannot reject the element for having the wrong type.
groups.equivalence_reason: Singleton; array integer validation is distinct from object-member validation.

groups.operation: Unpack a required object member.
groups.condition: The object lacks that member.
groups.capability: A format without the optional ? marker detects a missing required member.
groups.consequence: The fixed optional marker suppresses the missing-member rejection.
groups.equivalence_reason: Singleton; this concerns member presence.

groups.operation: Unpack an object in strict mode.
groups.condition: The input object has a member unconsumed by the format.
groups.capability: A strict object format or flag detects unconsumed members.
groups.consequence: The fixed {s?o} format does not reject the extra member.
groups.equivalence_reason: Both describe the same strict object-member check.

groups.operation: Unpack a typed object member.
groups.condition: The member's value conflicts with its selected typed format.
groups.capability: Typed validation reports expected and actual types with the member key.
groups.consequence: Generic o prevents the typed mismatch and its keyed diagnostic.
groups.equivalence_reason: Singleton; its typed-member condition is broader than the string-specific diagnostic claims.

groups.operation: Unpack a scalar with a typed format such as s, i, I, b, f, F, or n.
groups.condition: A scalar value is supplied for typed extraction or validation.
groups.capability: The selected scalar format extracts or validates its value.
groups.consequence: Generic o formats do not exercise typed scalar behavior.
groups.equivalence_reason: Singleton; this covers general scalar extraction and validation.

groups.operation: Recursively unpack a nested object or array.
groups.condition: An input value contains a nested structure.
groups.capability: A nested format selects recursive unpacking.
groups.consequence: Generic o at member and element positions does not recurse into the nested structure.
groups.equivalence_reason: Singleton; this concerns nested format dispatch.

groups.operation: Extract a JSON value with the O format.
groups.condition: A valid JSON value is selected for retained extraction.
groups.capability: O increments the extracted value's reference count.
groups.consequence: The fixed o formats exercise borrowed extraction only.
groups.equivalence_reason: Singleton; retained reference ownership is distinct from validation and diagnostics.

groups.operation: Unpack a typed object member and report its error through an unpack error destination.
groups.condition: A string format selects a non-string object member.
groups.capability: json_unpack_ex can report the member key in the wrong-type diagnostic.
groups.consequence: The keyed diagnostic is unavailable through the entry's generic o format and json_unpack call.
groups.equivalence_reason: All four target the same new key-bearing diagnostic for a typed member mismatch.

groups.operation: Unpack an object member with a string value format.
groups.condition: The selected member is not a string.
groups.capability: The string format rejects the member's type; {s?o} selects generic o instead.
groups.consequence: The wrong-type member is not rejected by string validation.
groups.equivalence_reason: These target the same object-member type check, independent of diagnostic wording.

groups.operation: Unpack an array element with i.
groups.condition: The selected element is not an integer.
groups.capability: i rejects the element's type; [o!] selects generic o instead.
groups.consequence: The non-integer element is not rejected by integer validation.
groups.equivalence_reason: Its array element and integer condition differ from the other typed-format claims.

groups.operation: Unpack a required object member.
groups.condition: The object lacks that member.
groups.capability: Object unpacking rejects a missing required member; ? makes data optional.
groups.consequence: The missing data member is not rejected as required.
groups.equivalence_reason: Both target the same missing-member check and optional-marker constraint.

groups.operation: Strictly unpack an object.
groups.condition: The object contains a member unconsumed by the format.
groups.capability: An object ! marker or strict unpack flag enables rejection; {s?o} and json_unpack do not enable it.
groups.consequence: The extra object member is not rejected by strict object validation.
groups.equivalence_reason: All three target strict rejection of unconsumed object members.

groups.operation: Extract or validate a scalar through a typed unpack format.
groups.condition: A scalar value is selected with a typed format.
groups.capability: Formats s, i, I, b, f, F, and n select typed scalar behavior; the entry selects o.
groups.consequence: Typed scalar extraction or validation is not reached.
groups.equivalence_reason: Both describe the same general typed-scalar dispatch gap.

groups.operation: Recursively unpack a nested object or array.
groups.condition: A selected member or element contains a nested structure.
groups.capability: Nested object or array formats descend into the value; o returns the value without descending.
groups.consequence: Recursive unpacking of the nested value is not reached.
groups.equivalence_reason: Both target recursive format dispatch for nested values.

groups.operation: Extract a JSON value with the O unpack format.
groups.condition: A valid selected value is unpacked with O.
groups.capability: O acquires a retained reference that must be released; the entry selects borrowed o.
groups.consequence: Retained-reference extraction and its ownership behavior are not reached.
groups.equivalence_reason: Both target the same O-format reference ownership contract.
